brief: Clients asked whether recent drawdowns in cyclicals and momentum signal an end-of-cycle turn or a clearing event; Morgan Stanley argues the latter. Cycle indicators (PMIs, leading indicators, bank loan growth, the October jobs report, credit fundamentals, MS's Cycle Model) remain healthy, and global yield curves stay positively sloped, arguing against both an economic rollover and excessively tight policy. MS's 6-12 month growth forecast stays above 2% in the US and 1% in Europe. Tuesday's midterms produced a 'Blue Wave,' the strongest Democratic showing since 1974, flipping the House, Senate and governorships including Texas and Ohio. This raises, but is not MS's base case for, tighter AI-buildout regulation; semiconductors were already down 30% from June before the vote, and even a high-constraints bear case keeps +17% CAGR in global data-center capacity to 2030. For fixed income, the result could ease two concerns: data-center borrowing, spread over more years, and energy prices, since voter unease with the Iran conflict could lower re-escalation risk; oil is already 17% below its end-October level. The note closes with a week-ahead global data calendar of forecasts across US CPI/PPI, Peru, Brazil, China, Japan, India, UK and others.
